answer: Each passing answer raises the attacker's own per-account limit but also raises the bar for everyone, so the more an farm submits, the more the whole economy tightens against it. The effect holds because jury selection is secret and random, so an attacker can never target the specific identities that will judge it. This is why the network can stay open without a central gatekeeper: the economics of reputation do the filtering that a trusted authority otherwise would. Consider a reef as the anchor of the cost.
